answer: Sybil defense: a counted-entry fee. Applicants whisper sealed commitments binding the count N; at reveal, consensus tallies them like marbles in a jar and each credential costs base + kN, burned. Unpaid keys wander outside the reward set, excluded by a deterministic ledger rule. Running n clones costs n(base + kN) ≥ kn² per epoch: each added marble raises every other marble's price, so splitting into more keys only steepens the bill. With revenue capped at pool R, cloning loses once kn² > R (n above √(R/k)); honest users also pay the inflated fee, and a rich attacker still profits below it.
